findings.finding: AC3 'corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only where obsolete' and AC4 'No load-bearing invariant is lost' rest on a correct-vs-delete judgment with no stated decision rule and no observable check; 'live/load-bearing invariant' is subjective as written, so the ACs are not deterministically evaluable.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the `reads_cli.py` '->CODE fix (extract one helper)' item with the parent's scope, which places code splits out of scope and defines only comment dispositions — either drop it to a comment-only disposition here or move the extraction to a separate code-change ticket outside this comment-triage shard.
evidence: Parent 373f description: 'Each shard identified the real call-graph seam instead, and those splits are out of scope here.'
Parent disposition vocabulary enumerates only comment dispositions (RELOCATE/DELETE/KEEP/DO_NOT_MOVE/CORRECT-IN-PLACE) — no code-change class.
Parent AC: 'No behaviour change: the full test suite AND `make lint` / `make typecheck` pass unchanged across every shard.'
Leaf's own headroom claims are careful to say '`WITHOUT any code extraction`', signalling code extraction is not this scope's remit.
findings.finding: The leaf's `_engine_support/reads_cli.py` item is a '->CODE fix (extract one helper)' — code refactoring/helper extraction — which steps outside the parent's comment-triage contract. The parent explicitly places code splits out of scope ('Each shard identified the real call-graph seam instead, and those splits are out of scope here') and its disposition vocabulary is comment-only (RELOCATE/DELETE/KEEP/DO_NOT_MOVE/CORRECT-IN-PLACE); a helper extraction also risks the parent's 'No behaviour change: the full test suite AND make lint / make typecheck pass unchanged' AC.
findings.location: Plan body: '`_engine_support/reads_cli.py` explains the same unknown-option rule in five near-identical blocks — a ->CODE fix (extract one helper) rather than a comment edit.'
scenarios: Implementer performs the helper extraction as part of this comment-triage shard, introducing a behaviour-adjacent code change the parent scoped out and that the parent's no-behaviour-change gate must catch.

findings.checklist_item: Specify that the reads_cli.py unknown-option helper must accept per-command usage/message text (and list's extra filters line) as parameters so each arm's distinct usage output is preserved byte-for-byte.
evidence: reads_cli.py _cmd_show prints usage 'ticket show ...', _cmd_list prints a distinct usage + a 'Valid filters:' line, _cmd_deps prints 'Usage: ticket deps <ticket_id> [--include-archived]', _cmd_ready prints 'ticket ready [--output json|llm] ...', _cmd_search prints 'ticket search <query> ...', _cmd_session_logs prints 'ticket session-logs ...' — the shared rule is only 'unknown option -> print error, print usage, return 2', but the usage text differs per arm
The plan calls this 'the same unknown-option rule in five near-identical blocks' but the blocks are near-identical only in the error line, not the usage payload
findings.finding: The reads_cli.py 'extract one helper' recommendation under-specifies the mechanism: the (six) unknown-option arms each emit a DIFFERENT usage string (and list emits an extra filters line), so a single naive helper cannot reproduce the per-command usage/error text without parameterization — flattening them would change user-facing usage output, colliding with the AC 'No load-bearing invariant is lost'.
findings.location: Plan paragraph: '_engine_support/reads_cli.py explains the same unknown-option rule in five near-identical blocks — a ->CODE fix (extract one helper)'
scenarios: Implementer extracts a helper that takes only argv/option and emits a single generic usage string, silently changing six commands' usage output
The parity/interface tests pin the exact usage strings and the extraction breaks them
findings.suggested_fix: Note in the plan that the extracted helper takes the usage string (and optional extra-lines) as arguments — e.g. `reject_unknown_option(arg, *usage_lines) -> int` returning 2 — so the six arms keep their distinct usage text.
